newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech house pauses in budget debate until 1615 GMT.
newsitem.headline: Czech house pauses in budget debate until 1615 GMT.

text.p: The Czech parliament has adjourned until 1815 local time (1615 GMT), ahead of an expected vote which may force the government to rework its 1997 draft state budget before submitting for a first reading later in October.

When debate resumes, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik and Budget Committee Chairman Jozef Wagner of the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) are scheduled to speak before a vote on the CSSD plan to force a reworking of the budget goes to a vote.

Earlier CSSD MP Stanislav Gross, submitted a plan which, in part, would require the government to re-submit its draft budget by the end of October with limits on the transfer of funds within the budget totals, once agreed in parliament.

It would also require a rise in payments to municipalities to compensate for changes in the tax code, and would limit the mayors of major cities to determine discressionary spending up to a maximum of 10 percent of state-provided funds.
The CSSD proposal must go to a vote before the budget draft, which was expected to have a first reading on Wednesday, can go to the floor.
However, under the rules of the parliament, a vote may not be taken in the plenary after 1900 local time (1700 GMT).
